content: When rifampin is discontinued, its effects on drug metabolism may persist for up to 14 days. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of warfarin by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Rifampin also decreases zaleplon levels by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism; caution and monitoring are advised. Similarly, rifampin reduces zidovudine levels by increasing its metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of ziprasidone, zolpidem, and zonisamide by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are required for these interactions. Additionally, rifampin reduces acetaminophen levels (oral, IV, and rectal) by increasing its metabolism, potentially leading to elevated hepatotoxic metabolites. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but caution is advised. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of aliskiren, alosetron, and alvimopan through mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters or hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. These interactions are considered minor, with unknown clinical significance. Rifampin also reduces ampicillin levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Bentonite decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. The clinical significance is minor and unclear. Rifampin reduces bisoprolol levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Similarly, rifampin decreases caffeine levels by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces celecoxib levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also decreases chloramphenicol and chlordiazepoxide levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces cimetidine levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Clofazimine decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces diazepam levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Similarly, rifampin decreases diclofenac levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces enalapril levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Ethanol decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Chronic ethanol use may increase the likelihood of this interaction. Rifampin reduces fexofenadine levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, with minor and unclear significance. Fluconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces flurbiprofen and fluvastatin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin decreases fosinopril levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also reduces frovatriptan levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin decreases ibuprofen levels (oral and IV) by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces imidapril levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also decreases isosorbide dinitrate and mononitrate levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Ketoconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces lansoprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It increases the effects of leflunomide by enhancing the metabolism of its active metabolite, with minor and unclear significance. Levoketoconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces levothyroxine and liothyronine levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also decreases lisinopril levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces loratadine levels through P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin decreases meloxicam levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Miconazole vaginally decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces modafinil levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin decreases moexipril and morphine levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also reduces nevirapine and nortriptyline levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin decreases ondansetron levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces opium tincture and oxacillin levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also decreases perindopril and pirmenol levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces piroxicam levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Posaconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin reduces quinapril levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also decreases rabeprazole levels by inducing CYP2C19 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces ramelteon and ramipril levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also decreases riluzole levels by inducing CYP1A2 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin reduces sulfamethoxazole levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Rifampin decreases thyroid desiccated and tibolone levels by increasing their metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. It also reduces trandolapril levels by increasing its metabolism, with minor and unclear significance. Voriconazole decreases rifampin levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption, but this applies only to oral forms of both agents. Rifampin significantly reduces the levels or effects of certain drugs, such as abemaciclib, abiraterone, abrocitinib, acalabrutinib, adagrasib, afatinib, and others, by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. In these cases, alternative drugs or close monitoring is recommended due to the potential for reduced efficacy or increased toxicity.
